raw_response:
I have been farming this land for 40 years. My father farmed before me. I know this soil. Every spring I think about the same things — how much fertilizer to buy, whether prices went up, what my neighbor Old Wang did last year that gave him a good harvest.

My 16 mu is divided the way I have always done it. About 12 mu I use for wheat and maize together — wheat in the autumn, maize after I cut the wheat in summer. The remaining 4 mu or so I put into stevia. The stevia buyer from the county town comes to my village every year, and the price is better than selling extra grain. My wife handles the drying.

**Wheat:** I plant every October. I use the Jimai variety — everyone in the village uses it now, and my yields have been solid, around 480 jin per mu on a good year. I converted to using 50 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base plus two 25 kg bags of urea split between winter and jointing stage. That comes out to roughly 14 kg of nitrogen per mu when I add it all up. I irrigate three times: once before it freezes, once at jointing, once when the heads come out. I spray once for weeds early on, then once more for rust or aphids near heading. I use rotary tillage after the maize comes off, then disc it before sowing.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest in June I go straight to maize seed. I use Xianyu 335 — the hybrid seed from the dealer. The seed cost is real money but the yield is much better than the old varieties my father used. I do no-till seeding right into the stubble now, saves fuel and the soil is already loose enough. I put 40 kg compound fertilizer at the bottom, then 30 kg urea split — half at planting, half when the plant is knee-high. Two irrigations if the summer rains are bad, otherwise maybe just one. Spray twice, once for stem borer early, once for leaf disease or aphids mid-season.

**Stevia:** This crop I know less deeply than wheat and maize, but I have grown it for 8 years now. I transplant seedlings in late April. I apply a bit less fertilizer than my grain crops — maybe 30 kg compound plus 20 kg urea through the season. The leaves need water though, I irrigate 5 times. I have to spray for insects a couple of times in summer. I harvest leaves twice a year, dry them on the courtyard. Last year I got about 200 kg dry leaves per mu. The buyer pays per jin.

I worry a bit about the stevia price dropping, but this year I will keep the same 4 mu in it. No reason to change what is working.
